q1_issues.issue: The adjective "popular" is dropped — no atom carries it, so the parse records only that hit men are a subject.
The complement "for TV movies" is dropped, leaving a kind-level claim at large, which is the same restriction-stripping the instruction set forbids for a PP that restricts a kind-level claim.
tv_movie is decomposed but appears in no other atom — an orphan genus for a symbol the parse never uses.

q2_gaps: an adjective inside a NOMINAL copular predicate that modifies the predicate role rather than the referent ("are a popular subject" does not make hit men popular) — fusing popular_subject is barred as incidental description, and the distributive/split route would assert the wrong thing, so there is no licensed encoding

a NOMINAL copular predicate carrying a PP complement at kind level ("a subject for TV movies") — state reification for a complement is defined only for an adjective's PP complement, and the fused adjective+bare-kind property (sensitive_to_light) is likewise adjective-only, so the "for" argument has no anchor
notes: The routing is right — bare-plural generic to Inheritance on hit_man at 0.9/0.9 with no QuantifierPhrase companion, and correct compound genus atoms with the noun modifiers left unexposed. But two of the three content elements of the predicate are missing, so the surviving atom is a much weaker and more general claim than the sentence makes.
